newsitem.title: UK: Mideast VLCCs stay flat despite good enquiry.
newsitem.headline: Mideast VLCCs stay flat despite good enquiry.

text.p: There was little relief for Middle East very large crude carriers (VLCC) rates on Thursday, with vessels continuing to be fixed below the W50 level to most destinations, brokers said.

Even a new ship, the 1996-built, 250,000 tonne Ohminesan, fetched only W47.5 to Japan for Idemitsu, while the 275,000 tonne Argo Hebe was fixed at the same rate from Ras Tanura to the U.S. Gulf for Exxon. "There has been a reasonable amount done but it's had no impact on rates. You can't keep having all this business and no impact.
"I'm surprised they haven't moved already...I'm expecting rates to move up soon," one optimistic broker said.
West Africa/U.S. Gulf rates, meanwhile, were steady, with VLCCs at W67.5 and 130,000 tonne vessels at W92.5, while North Sea/U.S. Atlantic Coast VLCCs were at W65 and million barrel ships at W92.5.

Rates in the Mediterranean stayed depressed, with 80,000 tonne vessels at W105/107.5, against W120 late last week and million barrel ships at W92.5. Inter-U.K./Cont rates were also weak, with 80,000 tonnes fixed at around W92.5, some 7.5 points down from last week. One dealer said cross-Med had fallen due to better interest in Med/Cont cargoes and a large number of re-lets on the market.
"We could see rates going down into the 80s next week," he said, adding that BP had come close to fixing a vessel at W87.5 although this was not the final rate.

Inter-U.K./Cont 25,000 fuel oil cargoes were flat at W185. One broker said, "There's enough enquiry to hold rates up at the moment. There are quite a lot of fixings out of the Baltic and I wouldn't be surprised to see rates creep up next week."
But in the Med there was enough tonnage around to keep a lid on rates at W195, he added.
Caribs/upcoast 70,000 tonne crude rates were little changed at W220 despite a falling off in enquiry in the last day or two, another broker said.

"Given the fall in enquiry, I'm surprised rates haven come off a bit, especially considering how high they are right now," he added, noting that rates are currently some 70 points above the 1996 average.
Caribs 50,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes were slightly firmer at W170.
